gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-ottom: Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq has a dignified, sizable lowercase whose bowls swell only slightly at their widest point. And Existence, the display heading, draws its lines without any such swell, so the eye never slows where the serif body does.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-sinha: Noto Serif Sinhala stands in a tall band of letters under short stalks, with strokes that vary just enough to feel alive. Make Existence small and its monoline build gets lost.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-telug: Lines like bent rope or tubing give Existence its look, with portholes for lowercase counters. But Noto Serif Telugu, a classic serif, tames the contrast and never goes razor thin, with tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-thai: Existence draws its letters like outlines traced in a single width, industrial and modern with wide porthole counters. Noto Serif Thai, a serif, lets its bodies dominate the line and swells measuredly from hairline to stem.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-tibet: Existence looks industrial, with porthole counters and constant-width arms and legs. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Serif Tibetan, a text serif, carries a moderate stroke shift you feel more than see.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-todhr: Tubular, porthole-eyed and unmistakably industrial. Existence traces each letter in a line of constant weight, while Noto Serif Todhri, a text serif, uses medium-range modulation and a sizable x-height for screen reading.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-toto: Rounded-wire strokes make Existence feel industrial and modern. Noto Serif Toto, a classic serif, adds a hulking lowercase like chalk pressed hard, with mild contrast that feels friendly.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-vithk: Neon-tube strokes, porthole counters, industrial through and through. Existence holds every line to one consistent thickness, while Noto Serif Vithkuqi, a classic serif, handles moderate thick-thin transitions and big round lowercase bowls.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-yezid: Noto Serif Yezidi reads as solid blocks of words, not skylines. A slight tug of heavier verticals against lighter horizontals separates it from Existence, whose letters are outlined at one steady thickness; I'd give the heading generous size.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-pt-serif-caption: Bent tubing meets bookish type here. Existence shapes its letters from one length of tube, and PT Serif Caption, a text serif, answers with a tall x-height and stems and hairlines in a close ratio.
